question: Should OpenClaw formally support `@openclaw/gateway-protocol` as a separately versioned public npm contract for third-party Gateway clients?
rationale: The patch is technically targeted, but publishing formerly private protocol exports establishes an ongoing compatibility and release-support obligation that implementation review alone cannot choose.

options.title: Approve the public package contract
options.body: Merge after confirming the documented entry points, calendar versioning, and release acceptance path are the intended supported contract for external clients.

options.title: Keep protocol distribution internal
options.body: Do not publish this package and continue exposing protocol integration only through the existing supported product surfaces.

options.title: Narrow the exported contract first
options.body: Publish only a deliberately stable subset after defining which schemas and helpers are supported for third parties.

recommendation.title: Approve the public package contract
recommendation.body: Merge after confirming the documented entry points, calendar versioning, and release acceptance path are the intended supported contract for external clients.

likelyOwner.reason: The supplied context identifies steipete as the trusted actor responsible for the package-publication and release-workflow design.
